activity.title: 👉 Multilingual students are often framed as needing to catch up. In reality, they’re already ahead. They’re navigating multiple languages, cultures, and ways of thinking…every single day. That’s not a gap. That’s an advantage. Let’s remind them (and us) that: • Language is strength • Identity is an asset • And belonging should be felt in every classroom 👉 If you work with multilingual learners, this matters. #future #innovation #education

“Word families” are not the same across languages. And that matters for how we talk about the Science of Reading. In English, word families are typically about sound patterns: cat, bat, hat They help students recognize rimes and decode efficiently. In Spanish, familias de palabras are about meaning and structure: pan, panadero, panadería They help students understand how words are built and how meaning travels across forms. Same term. Different linguistic logic. Here is where this connects to the Science of Reading. The Science of Reading is grounded in how reading develops within a language system. But when we move across languages, we are not just applying the same practices in translation. We are working across different orthographies, different linguistic structures, and different pathways to meaning. English opaque orthography needs pattern recognition to support decoding. Spanish is a more transparent orthography, where morphology and meaning are more consistently visible. So when we treat “word families” as equivalent across languages, we risk doing two things: • Importing English phonics practices into Spanish without alignment • Missing the opportunity to leverage the strengths of Spanish for vocabulary and meaning making For multilingual learners, this is not a small shift. It is the difference between teaching toward the structure of the language and teaching against it. A cross-linguistic Science of Reading asks us to be more precise: Not just “what works” But “what works, in which language, and why” Because biliteracy is not built through replication. It is built through alignment. #ScienceOfReading #Biliteracy #MultilingualLearners #LiteracyLeadership #EquityInEducation

Have you ever noticed how your tone and even your confidence can shift when you switch languages? Language shapes how we express tone, emotion, and connection. Bilingual speakers naturally adapt their communication style across languages. But this isn’t about becoming someone different. Language doesn’t change who you are—it gives you more ways to express yourself—more fully. In my work as a Spanish–English interpreter and translator, I see this every day. It’s not just about words—it’s about helping people fully show up, be understood, and connect with confidence. #Interpretation #Translation #Bilingual #LanguageAccess #CommunicationMatters #SpanishInterpreter #CulturalCompetence
This is very true. Interprtation goes far beyond just words and language.

Clear communication builds trust — especially when language differences are involved. At Pérez Language Solutions, I provide professional Spanish ↔ English interpretation and translation services to help organizations communicate accurately and respectfully with Spanish-speaking families, clients, and communities. Services include: • Educational interpretation (IEP meetings, conferences, school communication) • Business and community interpretation • Faith-based events and ministry support • Certified document translation • Professional written translation Professional interpreters and translators help ensure clarity, neutrality, and accuracy in important conversations. If your organization serves Spanish-speaking individuals and wants to strengthen communication and connection, I would love to connect. Tammy Pérez Pérez Language Solutions Bridging languages with excellence, integrity, and care.

Interpreter vs. Translator — what’s the difference? This question comes up often, and it’s a very common one. Both interpreters and translators support communication across languages, but they do so in slightly different ways: Interpreters work with spoken language • Meetings • Evaluations • Trainings • Conferences • Phone or virtual conversations Translators work with written documents • Birth and marriage certificates • Educational and legal documents • Forms, letters, and reports Both roles require specialized training, accuracy, and attention to confidentiality — and knowing which service is needed helps ensure communication is clear and complete. If you’re ever unsure whether interpretation or translation is the right fit for a particular situation, I’m always happy to help clarify or talk it through. — Tammy Pérez Spanish–English Interpreter & Translator Pérez Language Solutions Servicios de interpretación y traducción al español disponibles. #LanguageAccess #SpanishInterpreter #TranslationServices

Did you know that language access can look different depending on the situation? Many organizations do their very best to support Spanish-speaking families and clients by leaning on bilingual staff, volunteers, or trusted family members — especially during meetings, trainings, or important conversations. In some situations, however, having a professional interpreter or translator can provide additional clarity, confidentiality, and peace of mind for everyone involved. That’s where I’m honored to support organizations and individuals by offering professional Spanish ↔ English interpretation and translation. I work with: • Schools & districts • Businesses & organizations • Faith-based and community groups • Individuals needing certified document translation to help ensure communication is clear, respectful, and inclusive — so everyone can fully understand, participate, and feel heard. If your organization serves Spanish-speaking families, clients, or employees and is exploring ways to strengthen language access, I’d be happy to connect. 📩 I’m always glad to answer questions about: ✔ When professional interpretation may be helpful ✔ Ways to support Spanish-speaking families or clients ✔ Whether certified translation is needed for certain documents — Tammy Pérez Spanish–English Interpreter & Translator Pérez Language Solutions #LanguageAccess #SpanishInterpreter #CommunitySupport

I remember the day we bought our "$8k Lamborghini" In the early 90's our team and I had just launched the Leadership College and our budget was meager to say the least. Like trying to squeeze a dollar out of 15 cents! We had this vision to send teams into schools to talk to students about purpose and value, and no vehicle to actually get there. When our Finance Director called, they told us about an old 15 passenger Dodge van for sale at a mom-and-pop lot in Rockford. He figured the church could swing it cost wise, and when we pulled up that thing was U-G-L-Y. But it ran, and it drove well. $8K later, we pulled off the lot with it and we felt like purchased a Lamborghini. The vision now had a vehicle. Somebody helped us rig up a janky sound system and we were off to make a difference in as many student's lives as possible. One school booked us. Then another. And another. Our program interacted with over 1 million students during the next decade in large part to that ugly brown van, better known as our "$8K Lamborghini" Eventually our budget grew, better equipment followed, and our modes of transportation received a necessary upgrades. But here's what I learned: Big vision often begins with small steps God also honors those small and consistent steps of obedience and consistency...in church we'd call that "faithfulness to your calling". Maybe you find yourself walking this out today and I'd encourage you not to underestimate the seemingly small things like an act of obedience, a heartfelt prayer, or a necessary decision made. If you don't embrace the process, you'll never sustain the outcome. Be careful not to call something "insignificant" if God calls it a "beginning"
